# Part VI: Patterns and Anomalies {.unnumbered}

This part covers statistical modelling and machine learning, applied to audit. Some methods learn from past audit results, to predict which cases are risky: linear and logistic regression, decision trees and random forests. Others find structure in data without any past results: principal components, clustering and association rules. And others look for what does not fit: time series methods, anomaly detection, and data envelopment analysis for comparing the efficiency of units.

These methods rank and select; they do not prove. Every chapter shows how to turn their output into a list of cases to examine, and how to explain the selection.

The chapters in this part are:

- @sec-regression, linear regression, and expected values for comparison.
- @sec-logistic, logistic and multinomial regression for risk scoring.
- @sec-trees, decision trees, and the rules they find.
- @sec-forest, many trees voting, and what they reveal about risk.
- @sec-pca, reducing many indicators to a few, to see which hospitals stand apart.
- @sec-kmeans, grouping units by behaviour, and finding those that fit no group.
- @sec-apriori, association rules, including collusion in tenders.
- @sec-ts, time series: trend, seasons and forecasts.
- @sec-anomaly, anomaly detection, from boxplots to isolation forests and change points.
- @sec-dea, comparing the efficiency of health centres, depots and other units.
